title: Abelian model recognition from small cotorsion pairs
statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] in a fixed universe. Let $\mathcal Q,\mathcal W,\mathcal F$ be classes of its objects. A class is thick if it is closed under retracts and, in a short exact sequence, membership of any two objects implies membership of the third. For classes $\mathcal L,\mathcal T$, a cotorsion pair means $\mathcal L={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal T=\mathcal L^{\perp_1}$, where $\operatorname{Ext}^1(U,V)=0$ means every short exact sequence $0\to V\to E\to U\to0$ splits. It is complete if each $X$ occurs in exact sequences $0\to T\to L\to X\to0$ and $0\to X\to T'\to L'\to0$ with the indicated terms in the two classes. It is small if a set $I$ of monomorphisms with cokernels in $\mathcal L$ has as its right lifting class exactly the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal T$; a lifting class consists of maps against which every commutative square has a diagonal filler.

Suppose $\mathcal W$ is thick and $(\mathcal Q,\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W)$ and $(\mathcal Q\cap\mathcal W,\mathcal F)$ are complete small cotorsion pairs. There is a combinatorial abelian model structure on $\mathcal B$. Its cofibrations are precisely the monomorphisms with cokernel in $\mathcal Q$, its trivial cofibrations are those with cokernel in $\mathcal Q\cap\mathcal W$, its fibrations are precisely the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal F$, and its trivial fibrations are those with kernel in $\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W$. A morphism is a weak equivalence precisely when it factors as a trivial cofibration followed by a trivial fibration. Combinatorial here includes that $\mathcal B$ is locally presentable (cocomplete and generated under sufficiently filtered colimits by a set of sufficiently presentable objects), the two weak factorization systems are generated by sets, and both factorizations can be chosen functorially. A model structure means these two weak factorization systems, weak equivalences closed under retracts and satisfying two-out-of-three, and all small limits and colimits. A weak factorization system $(L,T)$ means every map factors as a map in $L$ followed by a map in $T$, and $L$ and $T$ are exactly each other's left and right lifting classes.

proof.text: Small colimits are part of [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Apply [lem-coef-grothendieck-small-limits] and [lem-coef-grothendieck-locally-presentable] with the same fixed universe to obtain all small limits and local presentability. Put $C=\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal Q)$, $C_0=\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal Q\cap\mathcal W)$, $R=\operatorname{Epi}(\mathcal F)$ and $R_0=\operatorname{Epi}(\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W)$; Mon and Epi specify, respectively, the indicated cokernel and kernel class.

proof.text: For either given cotorsion pair $(\mathcal L,\mathcal T)$, [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus] gives extension and retract closure, and zero membership, of both halves, and the lifting property of every $\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal L)$ against every $\operatorname{Epi}(\mathcal T)$. For composable monomorphisms $i:A\to B$ and $j:B\to D$, apply the snake lemma to the exact rows $A\xrightarrow{1_A}A\to0\to0$ and $B\xrightarrow{j}D\to\operatorname{Coker}j\to0$, with vertical maps $i,ji$ and $0:0\to\operatorname{Coker}j$. All three vertical kernels are zero, and the vertical cokernels are $\operatorname{Coker}i$, $\operatorname{Coker}(ji)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}j$. The cited six-term sequence, with its epic last arrow, therefore gives $0\to\operatorname{Coker}i\to\operatorname{Coker}(ji)\to\operatorname{Coker}j\to0$ directly. For composable epimorphisms $p:X\to Y$ and $q:Y\to Z$, apply the same cited snake statement to the rows $0\to X\xrightarrow{1}X\to0$ and $\operatorname{Ker}q\to Y\xrightarrow{q}Z\to0$, with vertical maps $0,p,qp$. Its exact sequence is $0\to\operatorname{Ker}p\to\operatorname{Ker}(qp)\to\operatorname{Ker}q\to0$, since $\operatorname{Coker}p=0$. Thus each of $C,C_0,R,R_0$ is composition closed. Each is retract closed: kernels and cokernels send retract diagrams of arrows to retract diagrams of objects, and monicity and epicity persist under arrow retracts.

proof.text: Here is the factorization for a complete cotorsion pair $(\mathcal L,\mathcal T)$. Given $f:A\to B$, choose $0\to A\xrightarrow{u}T_0\to L_0\to0$ by completeness. The graph $h=(f,u):A\to B\oplus T_0$ is monic. Let $D=\operatorname{Coker}h$, and choose $0\to T_1\to L_1\xrightarrow{v}D\to0$. Pull this sequence back along $B\oplus T_0\to D$ to form $E$. The pushout-of-short-exact-sequence theorem, applied in the opposite abelian category, gives $0\to T_1\to E\xrightarrow{e}B\oplus T_0\to0$. The graph lifts to $i:A\to E$ with zero $L_1$ component. It is monic and has cokernel $L_1$: the other pullback projection $E\to L_1$ has kernel $A$ and is epic, by the same opposite-category theorem applied to $0\to A\to B\oplus T_0\to D\to0$. Put $p=\operatorname{pr}_B e$, an epimorphism with $pi=f$. Pulling back $e$ to $T_0\subset B\oplus T_0$ identifies $\operatorname{Ker}p$ in $0\to T_1\to\operatorname{Ker}p\to T_0\to0$, so it lies in $\mathcal T$ by extension closure. This constructs a $\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal L)$--$\operatorname{Epi}(\mathcal T)$ factorization. Opposite-category use is legitimate: kernels become cokernels, monics become epics, and short exactness reverses.

proof.text: Together with lifting and retract closure, these factorizations give the exact lifting classes. If $f$ has the left lifting property against all $\operatorname{Epi}(\mathcal T)$, factor $f=pi$ as in Step 3 and use the square with top $i$, bottom identity, left $f$, right $p$. Its diagonal $s$ satisfies $sf=i$ and $ps=1$, making $f$ an arrow retract of $i$. If $f:A\to B$ has the right lifting property against all $\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal L)$, factor $f=pi$ with $i:A\to E$ and $p:E\to B$. Use the square with left side $i$, right side $f$, top $1_A$ and bottom $p$; its diagonal $r:E\to A$ satisfies $ri=1_A$ and $fr=p$. Thus $(i,1_B):f\to p$ and $(r,1_B):p\to f$ compose to the identity, so $f$ is an arrow retract of $p$. Therefore $(C,R_0)$ and $(C_0,R)$ are weak factorization systems. Smallness supplies sets $I,J$ with $I^{\square}=R_0$ and $J^{\square}=R$. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-small-object-factorization] using Step 1. Its left classes are ${}^{\square}R_0=C$ and ${}^{\square}R=C_0$ by the just-proved equalities. Hence both required factorizations can now be fixed functorially, and the systems are generated by the asserted sets.

proof.text: Define $V$ to be the composites $qj$ with $j\in C_0$, $q\in R_0$. For any factorization $f=qi$ with $i\in C$, $q\in R_0$, we claim $f\in V$ if and only if $\operatorname{Coker}i\in\mathcal W$. The reverse direction follows directly from the definition. For the forward direction write also $f=q'j$ with $j\in C_0,q'\in R_0$, and form $P=\operatorname{cod}(i)\times_{\operatorname{cod}(f)}\operatorname{cod}(j)$. The two projections are epic with kernels $\operatorname{Ker}q'$ and $\operatorname{Ker}q$, by the opposite-category form of [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence]. The diagonal $a:\operatorname{dom}(f)\to P$ is monic. The snake lemma on the two short exact rows with first vertical map identity gives, respectively, $0\to\operatorname{Ker}q'\to\operatorname{Coker}a\to\operatorname{Coker}i\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{Ker}q\to\operatorname{Coker}a\to\operatorname{Coker}j\to0$. The two kernels and $\operatorname{Coker}j$ lie in $\mathcal W$. Thickness first puts $\operatorname{Coker}a$ and then $\operatorname{Coker}i$ in $\mathcal W$. This proves the criterion for every such factorization, not merely the chosen one.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction before the displayed derived inverse limit; flat model recognition infrastructure, via lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model. Agent proof: factorization-independent cokernel criterion

proof.text: For $q\in R_0$ and any $h$ composable after $q$, we prove $hq\in V\Longleftrightarrow h\in V$. Write $h=sk$ with $k\in C,s\in R_0$ and $kq=tl$ with $l\in C,t\in R_0$. The square $tl=kq$ has horizontal monics $l,k$ and vertical epics $q,t$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-abelian] to the exact rows ending in their cokernels. It gives $0\to\operatorname{Ker}q\to\operatorname{Ker}t\to\operatorname{Coker}l\to\operatorname{Coker}k\to0$; the last arrow $\gamma:\operatorname{Coker}l\to\operatorname{Coker}k$ is epic because $\gamma\pi_l=\pi_k t$ and the quotient $\pi_k$ and $t$ are epic. Let $H$ be the image of $\operatorname{Ker}t\to\operatorname{Coker}l$. Then $0\to\operatorname{Ker}q\to\operatorname{Ker}t\to H\to0$ and $0\to H\to\operatorname{Coker}l\to\operatorname{Coker}k\to0$ are short exact. The two kernels lie in $\mathcal W$, so thickness puts $H$ there and shows $\operatorname{Coker}l\in\mathcal W$ if and only if $\operatorname{Coker}k\in\mathcal W$. Since $st\in R_0$ by Step 2, apply Step 5 to $h=sk$ and $hq=(st)l$. This proves the claimed cancellation equivalence without assuming two-out-of-three.

proof.text: For composable $f,g$, choose $f=qi$ and $gq=rj$ with $i,j\in C$ and $q,r\in R_0$. Then $gf=r(ji)$ with $ji\in C$. Step 5 gives $f\in V\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{Coker}i\in\mathcal W$, $gq\in V\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{Coker}j\in\mathcal W$, and $gf\in V\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{Coker}(ji)\in\mathcal W$. Step 6 replaces $gq\in V$ by $g\in V$. The snake-lemma short exact sequence $0\to\operatorname{Coker}i\to\operatorname{Coker}(ji)\to\operatorname{Coker}j\to0$ of Step 2 and thickness now prove all three implications of two-out-of-three for $V$. This covers arbitrary arrows; no monicity or epicity of $f,g$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the fixed functorial $(C,R_0)$ factorization from Step 4. A retract of arrows $f\to g\to f$ induces a retract of the corresponding left factors and therefore a retract $\operatorname{Coker}i_f\to\operatorname{Coker}i_g\to\operatorname{Coker}i_f$: the composite is identity because the factorization and cokernel assignments preserve identities and composition. If $g\in V$, Step 5 puts $\operatorname{Coker}i_g$ in $\mathcal W$; retract closure puts $\operatorname{Coker}i_f$ there, so $f\in V$. Thus $V$ is retract closed. This uses functoriality already established, not an unproved retract-closure theorem for a class of composites.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction before the displayed derived inverse limit; flat model recognition infrastructure, via lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model. Agent proof: explicit arrow-retract argument using Steps 4-5

proof.text: If $i\in C$, the factorization $i=1\,i$ and Step 5 give $i\in V$ exactly when $i\in C_0$, hence $C\cap V=C_0$. If $p\in R\cap V$, write $p=qj$ with $j\in C_0,q\in R_0$. Apply the snake lemma to the rows $A\xrightarrow{j}E\to\operatorname{Coker}j\to0$ and $B\xrightarrow{1}B\to0\to0$, with vertical maps $p,q,0$. Since $p,q$ are epic, this gives $0\to\operatorname{Ker}p\to\operatorname{Ker}q\to\operatorname{Coker}j\to0$. The last two objects are in $\mathcal W$, so thickness gives $\operatorname{Ker}p\in\mathcal W$, hence $p\in R_0$. Conversely $R_0\subset V$ by factoring with identity left factor, so $R\cap V=R_0$. Now the two systems of Step 4 are exactly the cofibration/trivial-fibration and trivial-cofibration/fibration systems; Steps 7-8 give the remaining weak-equivalence axioms, and Step 1 gives small limits and colimits. The cofibrant and fibrant objects are exactly $\mathcal Q$ and $\mathcal F$, since $0\to X$ has cokernel $X$ and $X\to0$ has kernel $X$. The acyclic objects are exactly $\mathcal W$: factor $0\to X$ as $0\to E\xrightarrow{q}X$ with $q\in R_0$; then $0\to\operatorname{Ker}q\to E\to X\to0$ and Step 5 show $0\to X\in V\Longleftrightarrow E\in\mathcal W\Longleftrightarrow X\in\mathcal W$. Local presentability, generating sets and functoriality have already been established in Steps 1 and 4, giving the claimed combinatorial abelian model structure and every specified class of maps.
